st.1: Banawali had no systematic drainage, unlike most Harappan towns.

x: All four statements are correct: Banawali lacked a systematic drainage; Lothal had mud-brick houses but burnt-brick drains; waste water went to soak pits or main channels; house drains joined covered street drains with manholes.

st.3: Lothal stands on the Bhogava, near the Gulf of Khambhat.

x: All three statements are correct: Mohenjodaro is in Larkana (Sindh), Banawali in Fatehabad (Haryana), and Lothal on the Bhogava in Gujarat.

st.3: Fire altars found at Kalibangan and Lothal suggest a Harappan fire cult.

x: All three statements are correct: the Great Bath was probably for ritual purification, yogic-pose figures suggest yoga, and fire altars at Kalibangan and Lothal point to a fire cult (not conclusive proof of the Vedic yajna).

st.3: It was later continued by Jonaraja and Srivara.

x: All three statements are correct: Kalhana wrote it in Sanskrit in the 12th century under Jayasimha, it has eight Tarangas, and it was continued by Jonaraja and Srivara.

st.3: The ASI began excavating Balirajgarh, a site with punch-marked coins, in Bihar.

x: All three statements are correct: a Satavahana-to-Vijayanagara field site was found in the Nallamala Tiger Reserve, Tamil-Brahmi trader names were found in the Valley of the Kings, and Balirajgarh (Madhubani) is in Bihar.

st.2: Katyayana wrote the Varttikas, a commentary on Panini's Ashtadhyayi.

x: All three statements are correct: Patanjali (Mahabhashya) was a contemporary of Pushyamitra Shunga, Katyayana wrote the Varttikas on Panini (the Nirukta is by Yaska), and Amarasimha was a navaratna of Chandragupta II.

st.3: The Yamuna is not mentioned at all in the Rigveda.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Yamuna is mentioned in the Rigveda (three times).
Both statements are correct: the Early Vedic economy was pastoral with yava (barley) as the main crop, while the Later Vedic economy became agrarian with rice (vrihi) and wheat (godhuma).

st.2: Among the Ikshvakus, the Ashvamedha brought the title Swarat.

x: All three statements are correct: the Satavahanas, Ikshvakus and Vishnukundins performed Vedic sacrifices; for the Ikshvakus the Ashvamedha gave Swarat (the Vajapeya gave Samrat); an Ashvamedha altar was found at Nagarjunakonda.

st.2: The Vaishya guilds (gana) were headed by a Shreshthin.

x: All three statements are correct: guild rules were Samay and Srenidharma, Vaishya guilds were headed by a Shreshthin (not a Gramani), and the Shatapatha Brahmana first mentions the usurer (kusidin).

st.2: Indra and Agni lost their earlier importance.

x: All three statements are correct: Prajapati became supreme, Indra and Agni declined in importance, and worship centred on costly sacrifices.

st.3: It is called Karmakanda.

x: All three statements are correct: Purva Mimamsa was founded by Jaimini, holds that liberation comes through ritual karma, and is the Karmakanda (Vedanta is the Jnanakanda).

st.3: Magga, the fourth truth, holds that the world is full of suffering.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Magga is the path (Eightfold Path) to end suffering; the truth that the world is full of suffering is Dukkha, the first truth.

st.3: Vesak (Buddha Purnima) commemorates the Buddha's birth, enlightenment and first sermon.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Vesak marks the Buddha's birth, enlightenment and death (mahaparinirvana), not the first sermon.

st.3: The Sautrantika school held that only consciousness is real.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the view that only consciousness is real belongs to the Yogachara (Vijnanavada) school; the Sautrantikas held that external objects are known only by inference.

st.2: The Kailasa temple at Ellora was carved under the Rashtrakuta king Krishna I.

x: All three statements are correct: Ellora has 17 Hindu, 12 Buddhist and 5 Jain caves, the Kailasa temple is a Rashtrakuta work of Krishna I, and the Udayagiri-Khandagiri caves are Jain.

st.2: The Gramika was a district-level officer.
st.3: The Rakshinas were in charge of the frontier forts.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Gramika was the village headman. Statement 3 is wrong: the Rakshinas were the police; frontier forts were under the Antapala.

st.3: The Hathigumpha inscription calls the Godavari 'Kannabenna'.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: 'Kannabenna' in the Hathigumpha inscription is the Krishna, not the Godavari.

st.2: The earliest surviving free-standing Hindu temples belong to the Kushana period.
st.3: The Dashavatara temple of Deogarh is in Kanpur district.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the earliest surviving free-standing temples are Gupta. Statement 3 is wrong: Deogarh is in Lalitpur district of Uttar Pradesh.

st.2: The Mrichchhakatika was written by Shudraka.

x: All four statements are correct: thirteen plays are attributed to Bhasa, the Mrichchhakatika is by Shudraka, the Devichandraguptam deals with Ramagupta and Dhruvadevi, and Rakshasa is Chanakya's rival in the Mudrarakshasa.

st.1: Pulakesin II defeated Harsha on the banks of the Narmada.

x: All four statements are correct: Pulakesin II of the Badami Chalukyas defeated Harsha on the Narmada, took the title Paramesvara, and the Aihole inscription records it.

st.2: Harshavardhana was its head.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: in Harsha's time Nalanda was headed by Silabhadra; Harsha was its patron.

st.2: The phase of the Slave dynasty under Iltutmish is called the Second Ilbari.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Iltutmish's line is the First Ilbari; the Second Ilbari is Balban's line.

st.2: The Qazi-ul-Quzat handled religious grants.
st.4: Turks and Indian Muslims intermarried freely.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: religious grants were under the Sadr-us-Sudur; the Qazi-ul-Quzat was the chief judge. Statement 4 is wrong: the Turkish nobility kept aloof and did not intermarry with Indian Muslims.

st.2: His Rihla was written in Persian.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Rihla was written in Arabic.

st.2: Mansabdari ranks were not hereditary and covered both civil and military duties.

x: All three statements are correct: the system had Central Asian roots, ranks were non-hereditary and both civil and military, and nobles' ranks ran from 10 to 5,000 with higher ones for princes.

st.3: The du-aspa sih-aspa system was introduced by Jahangir.

x: All four statements are correct: zat and sawar date from about 1595-96, equal sawar and zat meant the first class, du-aspa sih-aspa was Jahangir's, and dagh came in 1573-74.

st.2: For every 10 sawars a mansabdar had to keep 20 horses.
st.3: Nobles (umara) were mansabdars holding a rank of 1,000 sawar or above.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: sawar gave the cavalry to be kept and the rule was 20 horses per 10 sawars. Statement 3 is wrong: umara were mansabdars of 1,000 zat (not sawar) or above.

st.2: Tulsidas belonged to the Ramamargi branch of the Saguna stream.
st.4: The Dadu Panth was founded by Dadu Dayal in Punjab.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct: Tulsidas was a Rama bhakta of the Saguna stream. Statement 4 is wrong: Dadu Dayal founded the Dadu Panth in Rajasthan.

st.3: Nizamuddin Auliya lived at Delhi.

x: All three statements are correct: Baba Farid was Ganj-i-Shakar, Moinuddin Chishti's dargah is at Ajmer, and Nizamuddin Auliya lived at Delhi.
Both statements are correct: Rajaram created the post of Pratinidhi, and the Treaty of Warna (1731) settled Tarabai's line at Kolhapur.
Both statements are correct: Birsa Munda led the Munda Ulgulan, and Sidhu and Kanhu led the Santhal Rebellion (1855-56).
All three statements are correct: at Buxar (1764) the British defeated Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-Daula and Shah Alam II, and the Treaty of Allahabad followed in 1765.

All three statements are correct: Kandregula Jogipantulu used the Gollapudi pay mutiny to propose a Rs 15 lakh lease of the Circars, was made Majumdar of Rajamahendravaram by Nizam Ali, and received the title 'Raja Bahadur' from the British.

st.2: Kondapalli, also called Mustafanagar, was one of the Circars leased in 1766.

x: All three statements are correct: the 1766 Circars were Chicacole, Rajahmundry, Ellore and Mustafanagar (Kondapalli), while Guntur (Murtazanagar) was kept as Basalat Jang's estate; Kurnool was not one of them.

st.3: The bomb thrown at Lord Hardinge II during his state entry into Delhi (1912) was planned by Rash Behari Bose.

x: All three statements are correct: 1911 was the only Durbar attended by the monarch, the annulment and the capital shift were announced on 12 December 1911, and the 1912 Delhi bomb was planned by Rash Behari Bose (not the Chapekar brothers).

st.4: Revenue was not automatically remitted after a bad harvest; only occasional reductions were given.

x: All four statements are correct: the ryot could sell or mortgage land, assessment was revised about every 30 years, the first demand was 50 per cent of produce, and there was no automatic remission after a bad harvest.

st.3: The Noble School was founded before Madras University.

x: All three statements are correct: the Central Collegiate Institute (1841) preceded the Noble School (1843), which preceded Madras University (1857), which in turn came before result-based grants-in-aid.

st.3: The first railway line in Andhra (1862) was Puttur–Renigunta.

x: All three statements are correct: the 1853 train ran Bori Bunder–Thane, South India's first line (1856) was Royapuram–Wallajah Road, and Andhra's first (1862) was Puttur–Renigunta.

st.3: Jawaharlal Nehru formally joined it.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Nehru sympathised with the CSP but never formally joined it.
Both statements are correct: the federal dyarchy at the Centre never came into force, and the Act abolished the Council of India.

st.1: Gandhi's Harijan tour of November 1933 – July 1934, about 20,000 km, began from the Sabarmati Ashram.
st.2: Securing separate electorates for the depressed classes was one of the activities of the Harijan Sevak Sangh.

x: Statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the tour started from Wardha. Statement 2 is wrong: the Harijan Sevak Sangh worked against untouchability (education, temple entry, wells) and Gandhi opposed separate electorates.
Both statements are correct: Vivekananda spoke at the Chicago Parliament of Religions in 1893 and founded the Ramakrishna Mission in 1897.

st.2: Its founders were Madame H.P. Blavatsky and Colonel H.S. Olcott.

x: All four statements are correct: it was founded at New York in 1875 by Blavatsky and Olcott (Annie Besant joined later), came to India in 1879, and is called Divya Gnana Samajam in Telugu.

st.3: Its petitions protested against moturpha, a tax on land-revenue arrears.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: moturpha was a tax on professions, trades and houses, not on land-revenue arrears.

st.2: George Yule was the first European to be President of the Congress.

x: All four statements are correct: Tyabji was the first Muslim President (1887), George Yule the first European (1888, Allahabad), Sarojini Naidu the first Indian woman (1925), and Azad the youngest (1923).

st.2: It was originally planned for Poona but was shifted because of an outbreak of cholera there.

x: All three statements are correct: the 1885 session met at Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College, Bombay, after a cholera outbreak in Poona, and its delegates were mainly lawyers, journalists and teachers.

st.2: Separation of the judiciary from the executive was an administrative demand.

x: All four statements are correct: larger councils and budget control were constitutional demands, separation of the judiciary was an administrative demand, they protested the Natu brothers' deportation, and sought abolition of the salt tax.
All three statements are correct: Bhagat Singh was born in 1907, Chandrashekhar Azad in 1906 and Khudiram Bose in 1889.

st.3: His tomb is at Krishnadevipeta.

x: All four statements are correct: Alluri was born in 1897, nicknamed Chittibabu, shot at Koyyur and buried at Krishnadevipeta, and his biographer was Erramalli Narasimha Rao.

st.3: 'In Search of Gandhi' was written by Shyam Benegal.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: 'In Search of Gandhi' (1982) is by Richard Attenborough; Shyam Benegal made the film 'The Making of the Mahatma'.

st.4: Gandhi's booklet Constructive Programme was written by Vinoba Bhave.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: Constructive Programme (1941) was written by Gandhi himself, not Vinoba Bhave.

st.2: Its first session was presided over by Diwan Bahadur M. Ramachandra Rao.

x: All three statements are correct: the AISPC was organised by Balwantrai Mehta, Maniklal Kothari and G.R. Abhyankar, its first session was presided over by Diwan Bahadur Ramachandra Rao, and it was dissolved in 1948.

st.2: Mutual non-interference in each other's internal affairs is one of its principles.

x: Both statements are correct: non-aggression and non-interference in internal affairs are Panchsheel principles; collective military defence is not.

st.2: NTR's 1986 raising of the BC quota to 44% on the Muralidhar Rao Commission's report was upheld by the High Court.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: NTR's 44% BC quota (1986) was struck down by the High Court.

st.2: The formulation of the Tribal Panchsheel is credited to Verrier Elwin.

x: All four statements are correct: Nehru favoured integration, the Tribal Panchsheel is credited to Verrier Elwin (under Nehru's influence), Elwin's book argued for cultural autonomy, and PESA applies only to Fifth Schedule areas.

st.1: On 19 December 1952 Nehru announced an Andhra State excluding Madras city.

x: All three statements are correct: the fast began on 19 October 1952 at Bulusu Sambamurthy's house, Sriramulu died on 15 December 1952, and on 19 December Nehru announced an Andhra State without Madras city.

st.3: The Union Home Minister is the Vice-Chairman.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Union Home Minister is the Chairman of each Zonal Council; the Vice-Chairman is a Chief Minister by rotation.

st.3: Recruitment in Telangana required 12 years' residence.

x: All three statements are correct: Telangana's surplus was to be spent on Telangana with a five-year review, its students got at least one-third of technical seats, and recruitment needed 12 years' residence.

st.1: At least two of the portfolios of Home, Finance, Revenue, Planning & Development and Commerce & Industry were to go to Telangana.

x: All three statements are correct: at least two of the five key portfolios were to go to Telangana (not Home and Finance reserved), a 20-member Regional Council was set up with a ten-year review, and retrenchment and recruitment were proportionate.

st.2: Of the two new Union Territories, only Jammu and Kashmir has a legislature.

x: All three statements are correct: J&K and Ladakh became UTs on 31 October 2019, only J&K has a legislature (Ladakh has none), and India has 28 States and 8 UTs after the 2020 merger.

st.3: Megasthenes was the ambassador of Seleucus Nicator.

x: All three statements are correct: Megasthenes, envoy of Seleucus Nicator, says the Andhra king had 1,00,000 infantry and 1,000 elephants.
Both statements are correct: the Satavahana silver coin was the karshapana, and one gold suvarna equalled 35 karshapanas.

st.2: The Bhaja caves are earlier than the Karle chaitya.

x: All three statements are correct: rock-cut work peaked in the western Sahyadris, Bhaja is earlier than Karle, and eastern Deccan monuments are mostly structural with Guntupalli the rock-cut exception.

st.3: It was composed in Prakrit.

x: All three statements are correct: the Gathasaptasati of Hala opens with a prayer to Pasupati, is the main literary source on Satavahana society, and is in Maharashtri Prakrit, not Sanskrit.

st.3: Early Amaravati panels show the Buddha through symbols rather than in human form.

x: All three statements are correct: the Buddha was widely shown in human form under the Kushanas, Gandhara versus Mathura as the first is debated, and Amaravati's early panels used symbols.

All four statements are correct: Amaravati panels show the whole life of the Buddha, its Purna-kumbha is the AP State emblem, its crowded scenes include Yakshas and Gandharvas, and its slender figures are full of movement.

st.2: The Erragudipadu record of 575 CE is the first Telugu inscription.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the first Telugu inscription is the Kalamalla record of Dhanunjaya Varma; Erragudipadu is the first fully available Telugu record.

st.3: The accession of Durga Nripathi is recorded in the Kazipet (Dargah) inscription.

x: All three statements are correct: Rudradeva came to the throne in 1158, Kumaragiri Reddy in 1386, and the Kazipet inscription records Durga Nripathi's accession.

st.1: She was a sister of Ganapatideva.

x: Both statements are correct: Mailamba was Ganapatideva's sister (not daughter) and issued the Bayyaram tank inscription.

st.2: Kondavidu was gained by Ibrahim Quli Qutb Shah after 1565.

x: All three statements are correct: Sultan Quli built the Jama Masjid and was killed by Jamsheed, Ibrahim Quli Qutb Shah gained Kondavidu after 1565, and he built Golconda's high walls.

st.3: Its founder Tirumala Raya was the brother of Aliya Rama Raya.

x: All three statements are correct: the Aravidu was Vijayanagara's fourth dynasty, named after Araviti in Kurnool, and was founded by Tirumala Raya, brother of Aliya Rama Raya.

st.2: He was defeated at Vandavasi (1642) by Ibrahim Qutb Shah.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Sriranga III was defeated by Bijapur and Golconda forces (Mir Jumla); Ibrahim Qutb Shah ruled a century earlier (1550-80).
All three statements are correct: Kakatiya temples had monasteries and feeding houses, Kalamukhas gave anna dana, and temple women sustained dance and music.

st.3: The Bala Bharati Samiti was founded at Rajahmundry in February 1907 by local youths such as Chilukuri Veerabhadra Rao.

x: All four statements are correct: Banerjea's arrest set off protests across Andhra under 'Vandemataram – Manade Rajyam', and the Bala Bharati Samiti was founded at Rajahmundry in 1907 by youths such as Chilukuri Veerabhadra Rao, with backing from Karanam Guneswara Rao.

st.1: At the AICC meeting there, Gandhi's speech was translated into Telugu by Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao.

x: All three statements are correct: Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao translated Gandhi's speech, the APCC met in January 1921, and the AICC met on 31 March – 1 April 1921.

st.2: He won the Sahitya Akademi award for Kreestu Charitra.

x: All three statements are correct: Gabbilam (1941) has a bat carry a Dalit's message, Jashuva won the Sahitya Akademi award for Kreestu Charitra (not Gabbilam), and he was called Viswakavi Samrat.

st.1: Vyavahara Dharmabodhini was written by Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Vyavahara Dharmabodhini was written by Kandukuri Veeresalingam.

st.2: The Kakinada Samajam (1885) was founded by Danavahi Hanumantharao.

x: All three statements are correct: the Guntur Samajam (1880-81) was the earliest, the Kakinada Samajam (1885) was Danavahi Hanumantharao's, and Rajahmundry's staged Chilakamarti's and Toleti's plays; Immani Hanumantharao founded the Rajahmundry Samajam.

st.3: Any group of ten youths opening a village library received his paper, books and Bharati free.

x: All four statements are correct: Kasinathuni funded his work from Amrutanjan, named Andhra Granthamala to popularise 'Andhra', gave free material to any ten youths opening a library, and finished Velidanda Hanumantha Rao's catalogue.

st.2: He edited the Andhra Patrika from 1916 to 1918.

x: Both statements are correct: Harisarvottama Rao signed the Sreebagh Pact and edited the Andhra Patrika (1916-18); Grandhalaya Sarvasvam was Ayyanki Venkataramanaiah's journal.

st.1: He hoped that Article 352 would remain a 'dead letter'.
st.4: He held that as India was a 'Union of States', the states had a right to secede.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Ambedkar's 'dead letter' hope was about Article 356, not 352. Statement 4 is wrong: he said the Union was indestructible and no state had a right to secede.

st.3: He sent his physician Jivaka to Ujjain to treat Prasenajit for jaundice.
st.4: His physician Jivaka was the son of the Vaishali courtesan Amrapali.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Jivaka treated Pradyota of Avanti. Statement 4 is wrong: Jivaka was the son of Salavati, a courtesan of Rajagriha.

st.2: It was carved top-down from a single basalt cliff.

x: All three statements are correct: the Kailasa is Cave 16, carved top-down from a single basalt rock (not granite), with a Dravida vimana.

st.2: Temple building in Andhra began under the Ikshvakus.

x: Both statements are correct: the Parasurameswara temple at Gudimallam is the oldest Saivite temple, and temple building in Andhra began under the Ikshvakus.

st.3: The Nalayira Divya Prabandham, with 4,000 verses of the 12 Alvars, was compiled by Nambi Andar Nambi.
st.4: The Saiva canon Tirumurai was compiled in the time of Kulottunga I.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Divya Prabandham was compiled by Nathamuni. Statement 4 is wrong: Nambi Andar Nambi compiled the Tirumurai in the time of Rajaraja I.

st.3: The Jain Kirti Stambha, built by the merchant Jijaji in the 12th century, is dedicated to Mahavira.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Jijaji's Jain Kirti Stambha is dedicated to Adinath.

st.4: For Mills, an economic slowdown is a personal trouble while one person's unemployment is a public issue.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: for Mills one person's unemployment is a personal trouble, while mass unemployment in a slowdown is a public issue.

st.1: The 2005 amendment made daughters coparceners by birth under Section 14.
st.2: In Vineeta Sharma (2020), the Supreme Court held that this applies only if the father was alive in 2005.

x: Statements 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: daughters were made coparceners under Section 6. Statement 2 is wrong: Vineeta Sharma held the right applies whether or not the father was alive in 2005.

st.1: Irawati Karve's 'Kinship Organization in India' (1953) divided India into four kinship zones – North, Central, South and West.
st.3: Louis Dumont wrote 'Regional Variations in Hindu Kinship' (1968).

x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Karve's four zones were North, Central, South and East. Statement 3 is wrong: 'Regional Variations in Hindu Kinship' (1968) is by Pauline Kolenda.

st.2: Varna refers to the real local groups of the caste system, numbering thousands of sub-castes.
st.3: The 1931 Census recorded 4,147 castes, and it was the first Census to enumerate caste.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the real local groups are jatis; varna is the four-fold scheme. Statement 3 is wrong: caste enumeration began with the 1871 Census.

st.3: Totemism, a clan's sacred bond with an animal or plant totem, goes with clan endogamy.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: totemism goes with clan exogamy.

st.1: The Sahariyas are the smallest PVTG by population.
st.3: The Dongaria Khond and Kutia Khond are not on the joint Andhra Pradesh–Telangana PVTG list.

x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Sahariyas are the largest PVTG (the Sentinelese the smallest). Statement 3 is wrong: Dongaria Khond and Kutia Khond are on the joint list of 12.

st.2: The Constitution (131st) Amendment Bill, 2026 was passed on 17 April 2026.
st.4: Andhra Pradesh reserves 50% of seats in panchayats but not in municipalities for women.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the 131st Amendment Bill was defeated on 17 April 2026. Statement 4 is wrong: AP reserves 50% of seats for women in both panchayats and municipalities.

st.1: A majority of Indian marriages are now inter-caste.
st.3: The Supreme Court upheld the UGC (Promotion of Equity in HEIs) Regulations, 2026 without any stay.

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: only about 5% of marriages are inter-caste. Statement 3 is wrong: the Supreme Court stayed the UGC Regulations, 2026.

st.2: Uttar Pradesh has the highest share of SCs in its population.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Punjab has the highest SC share; Uttar Pradesh has the largest SC number.

st.2: The Karnataka Bill punishes only individuals, with no organisational liability.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Karnataka Bill provides 2-10 years and also makes organisations liable.

st.1: The 2017 amendment makes a crèche mandatory in every establishment, whatever the number of employees.
st.3: The Code on Wages, 2019 subsumes the Maternity Benefit Act.

x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: a crèche is mandatory only in establishments with 50 or more employees. Statement 3 is wrong: the Maternity Benefit Act is subsumed in the Code on Social Security, 2020.

st.1: According to the Study on Child Abuse: India 2007, conducted by the NCRB, two out of three children faced physical abuse.
st.3: As per NCRB 2021, 97.1 per cent of child sexual-abuse offenders were strangers to the child.
st.4: As per NCRB 2023, Assam recorded the highest number of crimes against children.

x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the 2007 study was by the Ministry of Women and Child Development, not the NCRB. Statement 3 is wrong: 97.1 per cent of offenders were known to the child. Statement 4 is wrong: Madhya Pradesh had the highest number; Assam had the highest rate.

st.2: It was constituted on 21 August 2020, before the 2019 Act came into force.
st.3: It is chaired by the Chairperson of the NHRC.
st.4: Its non-official members are elected by Parliament.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Act came into force in January 2020, before the Council was constituted in August 2020. Statement 3 is wrong: it is chaired by the Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment. Statement 4 is wrong: non-official members are nominated by the Centre for a term of 3 years.

st.2: The farmer premium is the same for kharif, rabi and commercial crops.
st.3: There is an upper limit on the Government's premium subsidy.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the farmer premium differs – 2% kharif, 1.5% rabi, 5% commercial and horticultural crops. Statement 3 is wrong: the Government pays the balance with no upper limit on the subsidy.

st.1: AP's YSR Rythu Bharosa gave ₹13,500 a year per acre.

x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: YSR Rythu Bharosa gave ₹13,500 a year per farmer family; the per-acre payment is Telangana's.

st.3: Its successor Annadata Sukhibhava gives ₹20,000 a year, entirely from the State's own funds.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Annadata Sukhibhava's ₹20,000 is ₹14,000 from the State plus ₹6,000 from PM-KISAN.

st.1: The term 'minority' is defined in Article 366 of the Constitution.
st.3: Under Section 2(c) of the NCM Act, 1992, a minority is a community notified as such by the State Government.
st.4: After the T.M.A. Pai case (2002), minority status is decided with reference to the national population.

x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Constitution does not define 'minority'. Statement 3 is wrong: under Section 2(c) the Central Government notifies minorities. Statement 4 is wrong: after T.M.A. Pai minority status is decided State-wise.

st.2: Its Chairperson must be a retired judge of the Supreme Court.
st.4: It decides the minority status of educational institutions but has no civil court powers.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Chairperson must have been a High Court judge. Statement 4 is wrong: the NCMEI decides minority status and issues certificates with the powers of a civil court.

st.4: The 25th round of Special Representatives' talks (August 2026) was held in New Delhi.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: the 25th round (August 2026) was held in Beijing; the 24th was in New Delhi.

st.1: The Kaladan Multi-Modal Transit Transport Project links Kolkata with Mizoram through Chittagong port.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Kaladan project runs through Sittwe port in Myanmar, not Chittagong.

st.3: Iran, India's largest socio-economic partner in West Asia, hosts an Indian diaspora of about 10 million.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: it is the GCC, not Iran, that is India's largest socio-economic partner in West Asia, with about 10 million Indians.

st.1: The Kudankulam nuclear power plant, built with Russian cooperation, is in Andhra Pradesh.

x: Statements 2, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Kudankulam is in Tamil Nadu.

st.3: The India-EU FTA was concluded at the 16th India-EU Summit (2026), held in Brussels.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the 16th Summit (2026) was held in India, and the FTA made the EU India's 22nd FTA partner.

st.3: The World Food Programme was founded in 1961 and is headquartered at Geneva.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the WFP is headquartered at Rome.

st.2: The EXIM Bank of India, established on 1 January 1982, is headquartered at New Delhi.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the EXIM Bank is headquartered at Mumbai.

st.1: Constitutionalism is inherent in every constitution.
st.3: The Indian Constitution is as rigid as the US Constitution.

x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: having a constitution does not guarantee constitutionalism (limited government). Statement 3 is wrong: the Indian Constitution is a blend of rigidity and flexibility.

st.2: The Constitution now has about 470 Articles, 25 Parts and 12 Schedules, the number of Schedules being unchanged since 1950.
st.4: The framers studied only the British and US constitutions.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Schedules have grown from 8 to 12. Statement 4 is wrong: the framers studied the constitutions of about 60 countries.

st.3: After partition its strength was unchanged at 389.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: after partition its strength fell to 299.

st.3: The impeachment of the President was borrowed from Britain.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: impeachment of the President was borrowed from the USA.

st.2: An Agiary is a Tower of Silence.
st.3: Shahenshahi is the highest grade of fire temple.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: an Agiary is a fire temple; the Tower of Silence is the Dakhma. Statement 3 is wrong: the highest grade of fire temple is the Atash Behram; Shahenshahi is a Parsi calendar sect.

st.3: The international instrument prohibiting it is the UN Charter.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: child labour is dealt with by ILO Conventions 138 and 182 (and the UNCRC), not the UN Charter.

st.2: It was based on the recommendations of the Santhanam Committee.
st.3: It inserted 'Socialist' and 'Secular' between 'Democratic' and 'Republic'.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the 42nd Amendment was based on the Swaran Singh Committee. Statement 3 is wrong: 'Socialist' and 'Secular' were inserted between 'Sovereign' and 'Democratic'.

st.2: The Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act, 2019 makes instant triple talaq only a civil wrong, not a criminal offence.
st.4: In Supriyo (October 2023), the Supreme Court recognised a Fundamental Right of same-sex couples to marry.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the 2019 Act makes instant triple talaq a criminal offence punishable with up to three years. Statement 4 is wrong: in Supriyo the Court refused to recognise a Fundamental Right to marry.

st.1: The safeguards in D.K. Basu (1997) relate mainly to bail for under-trial prisoners.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the D.K. Basu guidelines relate to arrest and custodial detention.

st.2: It operates within the 50 per cent ceiling on reservation.
st.3: It is mandatory for the States.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the 10% EWS quota is over and above the 50 per cent ceiling. Statement 3 is wrong: it is an enabling provision, not mandatory.

st.1: It was adopted by the UN Security Council on 20 November 1989 and has 54 articles.

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the CRC was adopted by the UN General Assembly. Statement 3 is wrong: India is not a party to the 2011 Optional Protocol on a communications procedure.

st.4: It extended the term of the Lok Sabha but not of the State Assemblies to six years.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: the 42nd Amendment extended the term of both the Lok Sabha and the State Assemblies to six years.

st.2: A State law reserved for and assented to by the President under Article 254(2) becomes permanently immune from any later law of Parliament.
st.3: Article 254(2) applies to State List matters as well.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Parliament can later amend or repeal such a State law. Statement 3 is wrong: Article 254(2) applies only to Concurrent List matters.

st.2: A Governor appointed as administrator of an adjoining Union Territory acts on the advice of his State Council of Ministers.
st.3: Lakshadweep is administered by the Governor of Kerala.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: as administrator the Governor acts independently of his Council of Ministers. Statement 3 is wrong: Lakshadweep has an Administrator appointed by the President.

st.2: Prorogation by the President ends both the session and the life of the House.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: prorogation ends only the session; dissolution ends the life of the House.

st.2: The Committee on Public Undertakings was created in 1964 on the recommendation of the Ashok Mehta Committee.
st.3: The Public Accounts Committee is described as a 'continuous economy committee'.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the COPU was created on the recommendation of the Krishna Menon Committee. Statement 3 is wrong: the 'continuous economy committee' is the Estimates Committee.

st.1: His emoluments are determined by Parliament by law and are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.
st.3: A member of the State Legislature appointed Governor may keep his seat in the Legislature.

x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Governor's emoluments are charged on the Consolidated Fund of the State. Statement 3 is wrong: such a member is deemed to have vacated his seat on becoming Governor.

st.1: High Court judges are appointed by the Governor of the State.
st.2: For the appointment of a Supreme Court judge other than the CJI, consultation with the Chief Justice of India is optional.
st.4: The 'distinguished jurist' route has been used to appoint a Supreme Court judge.

x: Statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: High Court judges are appointed by the President. Statement 2 is wrong: consultation with the CJI is obligatory. Statement 4 is wrong: the 'distinguished jurist' route has never been used.

st.1: The Preamble describes India as a quasi-federal State.
st.3: Harold Laski described Indian federalism as 'cooperative federalism'.

x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Preamble does not use 'federal' at all; 'quasi-federal' is K.C. Wheare's description. Statement 3 is wrong: 'cooperative federalism' is Granville Austin's phrase.

st.1: Kerala argued that it enters Union List Entries 18 and 50.

x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Kerala argued that the Bill enters State List Entries 18 and 50.

Both statements are correct: executive power in Concurrent List subjects rests with the States by default, and the Centre executes such subjects only where the Constitution or a Parliamentary law expressly provides.

st.2: During the Supreme Court inquiry into misbehaviour, a member of a State PSC may be suspended only by the President.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: during the inquiry a State PSC member is suspended by the Governor (removal is by the President).

st.1: The Universal Periodic Review, a peer review of every UN member's record, is conducted by the UN Security Council.
st.2: Special rapporteurs under the special procedures are paid UN staff.

x: Statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the UPR (from 2008) is run by the UN Human Rights Council. Statement 2 is wrong: special rapporteurs are unpaid independent experts.

st.2: Under Article 161 the Governor can pardon a death sentence.
st.4: Murder (old IPC s.302) is now punished under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: only the President (Article 72) can pardon a death sentence. Statement 4 is wrong: murder is punished under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (s.103); the BNSS is the procedure code.

Both statements are correct: the 2019 amendment let the Centre fix the tenure and salaries of Information Commissioners, and Section 44(3) of the DPDP Act, 2023 amended Section 8(1)(j) of the RTI Act.

st.2: The 16th Finance Commission (2026-31) is chaired by N.K. Singh.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the 16th Finance Commission is chaired by Arvind Panagariya; N.K. Singh chaired the 15th.

st.2: The VB-G RAM G Act replaced MGNREGA and reduces the States' share of funding.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the VB-G RAM G Act raises the States' share of funding.

All three statements are correct: Laxmikanth lists the Akali Dal, DMK, TDP and AGP as culture- or ethnicity-based, the BJD, RJD, TMC and YSRCP as splits from national parties, and regional neglect and unmet aspirations as causes.

st.2: Under the 2002 Act it is chaired by a retired High Court judge.
st.4: It redraws constituencies on the basis of the latest electoral rolls.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Delimitation Commission is chaired by a retired Supreme Court judge. Statement 4 is wrong: it redraws constituencies on the basis of the census.

st.2: NOTA is equivalent to abstention.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: a NOTA vote is a recorded, active choice, not abstention.

st.1: A five-judge bench upheld the Electoral Bond Scheme but ordered disclosure of donors.
st.4: The Reserve Bank of India was directed to give the donor data to the Election Commission.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the five-judge bench unanimously struck down the scheme. Statement 4 is wrong: the State Bank of India was directed to give the data.

st.3: The Gandhian Plan of 1944 was prepared by J.C. Kumarappa.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Gandhian Plan (1944) was prepared by Shriman Narayan Agarwal.

st.1: Part IX-A, Articles 243 to 243O, of the Constitution.
st.4: Regular remuneration to members of panchayats.

x: Items 2 and 3 are provisions of the 73rd Amendment. Item 1 is wrong: Articles 243 to 243O form Part IX (Part IX-A is the municipalities). Item 4 is wrong: the Amendment does not provide regular remuneration to panchayat members.

st.1: The first Municipal Corporation in India was set up at Calcutta in 1726.
st.4: The AP Urban Water Supply Project covering 50 ULBs is aided by the World Bank.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the first Municipal Corporation was at Madras (1688). Statement 4 is wrong: the project is aided by the AIIB.

st.2: Stabilisation measures were long-term and aimed at raising industrial productivity.
st.3: Devaluation of the rupee was a structural-adjustment measure.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: stabilisation measures were short-term, aimed at the balance of payments, inflation and fiscal deficit. Statement 3 is wrong: devaluation was a stabilisation measure.

st.1: MUDRA stands for Micro Units Development and Regulatory Agency.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: MUDRA is the Micro Units Development and Refinance Agency.

st.2: Adjudicating telecom disputes and appeals is a function of TRAI.
st.3: TDSAT (May 2000) was created by a separate TDSAT Act, 2000.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: disputes and appeals go to TDSAT, not TRAI. Statement 3 is wrong: TDSAT was created by the 2000 amendment to the TRAI Act.

st.3: The overdraft limit has been raised from ₹5,000 to ₹10,000 and is open to account holders of any age.
st.4: After 14 August 2018 its focus shifted from every unbanked adult to every household.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the overdraft (now ₹10,000) has an age limit (18-65). Statement 4 is wrong: the focus shifted from every household to every unbanked adult.

st.2: With a score of 74 in the SDG India Index 2023-24, Andhra Pradesh is an Achiever.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: a score of 74 puts AP among the Front Runners (65-99); only 100 is the Achiever band.

st.2: Fully disabled persons get the same amount as other disabled persons.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: fully disabled persons get ₹15,000 a month, more than the ₹6,000 for other disabled persons.

st.2: The AP Assembly resolution asking for the words 'at Amaravati' in Section 5(2) was passed on 28 March 2026.

x: All four statements are correct: the common capital ended on 2 June 2024, the Assembly resolution on 'at Amaravati' was passed on 28 March 2026, the 2026 Amendment Act was the first in which Parliament named a State's capital, and the Sivaramakrishnan Committee was set up under Section 6.

st.2: The 21.4% primary share excludes mining, so it is directly comparable with the old agriculture-forestry-fishing share.
st.4: Compared with the old series, the new series shows lower agriculture and industry shares and a higher services share.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the primary share includes mining, so it is not comparable with the old agriculture share. Statement 4 is wrong: the new series shows higher agriculture and industry shares and a lower services share.

st.2: It defined the unorganised sector as incorporated companies with fewer than 10 workers.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the NCEUS defined the unorganised sector as unincorporated enterprises of individuals or households with fewer than 10 workers.

st.3: The same study found manufacturing to be the most employment-intensive sector.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the RBI study found construction and services to be the most employment-intensive.

st.2: A higher ICOR indicates more efficient investment.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: a higher ICOR means more capital per unit of output, i.e. less efficient investment.

All three statements are correct: AP's HCR in 2011-12 was 9.20% against India's 21.92%, HCES 2022-23 was the first full MPCE update in over a decade, and Tendulkar-line poverty was about 4.7% (2022-23) and 2.3% (2023-24).

st.1: The National Planning Committee estimated a subsistence line of ₹16-35 per capita per year at 1867-68 prices.
st.3: The Planning Commission Working Group of 1962 was the first to use a calorie norm for the poverty line.

x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the ₹16-35 estimate at 1867-68 prices was Dadabhai Naoroji's; the National Planning Committee (1938) gave ₹15-20 a month. Statement 3 is wrong: the 1962 group fixed ₹20/₹25 a month; Dandekar and Rath (1971) first used calories.

st.2: The IBBI adjudicates insolvency cases, while the NCLT regulates the process.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the NCLT adjudicates insolvency cases, while the IBBI regulates the process.

st.2: The Act requires its Chairman to have experience in judicial service.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Chairman must have experience in public affairs; judicial qualification applies to one of the members.

st.2: It retained the distinction between general and Special Category States.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the 14th Finance Commission did away with the distinction between general and Special Category States.

st.2: The Gadgil Formula, which gave SCS States a reserved share of Normal Central Assistance, was approved by the Finance Commission.
st.3: SCS is expressly provided for in the Constitution.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Gadgil Formula was approved by the National Development Council. Statement 3 is wrong: SCS has no constitutional provision.

st.3: The 14th Finance Commission's recommendations were rejected by the Union Government.
st.4: The 16th Finance Commission added a 'Contribution to GDP' criterion and continued revenue deficit grants.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the 14th FC's recommendations were accepted on 24 February 2015. Statement 4 is wrong: the 16th FC added 'Contribution to GDP' (10% weight) but ended revenue deficit grants.

st.1: Its Cabinet resolution fixes the number of full-time members at five.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the number of full-time members is not fixed (three in 2015, seven from June 2026).

st.2: It must change its promoters.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: a small finance bank moving to a universal bank need not change its promoters.

st.1: Budget 2021-22 announced the privatisation of two PSBs and the LIC.
st.3: Only the Government, not LIC, is selling its stake in IDBI Bank.
st.4: Trade unions argue that privatisation would strengthen priority-sector lending and rural credit.

x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Budget 2021-22 announced the privatisation of two PSBs and one general insurance company. Statement 3 is wrong: both the Government and LIC are selling stakes in IDBI Bank. Statement 4 is wrong: unions argue privatisation would weaken priority-sector and rural lending.

st.2: The Code's deterrent effect is seen in cases being settled only after liquidation.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the deterrent effect shows in many cases being settled before admission.

st.2: Revenue expenditure has risen from 77% of total expenditure (2014-15) to about 88%.
st.3: Capital expenditure is the largest block of Union spending.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: revenue expenditure has fallen from 88% (2014-15) to about 77%. Statement 3 is wrong: revenue expenditure, not capital expenditure, is the largest block.

st.3: The new 50 ± 1% target by 31 March 2031 was set by the 16th Finance Commission.
st.4: Budget 2026-27 made the fiscal deficit replace the debt-GDP ratio as the principal fiscal anchor.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the 50 ± 1% target was set by the Union Government in the Budget. Statement 4 is wrong: the debt-GDP ratio replaced the fiscal deficit as the anchor.

st.2: Capital expenditure is larger than interest payments.
st.3: The fiscal deficit of 4.3% of GDP is higher than the 2024-25 level.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: capex (₹12.22 lakh crore) is below interest payments (about ₹14.04 lakh crore). Statement 3 is wrong: 4.3% is lower than the 4.8% of 2024-25.

st.3: It is to be based mainly on wider use of chemical pesticides.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Second Green Revolution stresses sustainable, resource-conserving farming, not more chemical pesticides.

st.3: The Intensive Agricultural Area Programme (1964-65) was confined to the original 7 IADP districts.
st.4: HYV seeds were first introduced in India under the IADP itself in 1960-61.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the IAAP extended the approach to 114 districts. Statement 4 is wrong: HYV seeds came later, in the Kharif season of 1966.

st.1: It was launched in 2015 at Suratgarh, Punjab.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Suratgarh is in Rajasthan.

st.2: The Indian Institute of Maize Research is located at Hyderabad.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Indian Institute of Maize Research is at Ludhiana.

st.3: Less than half of agricultural households in AP are indebted (NSSO 77th round).
st.4: A NABARD study found that AP farmers depend on institutional credit alone.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: 93.2% of AP agricultural households are indebted, the highest in India. Statement 4 is wrong: about 50% of AP farmers depend on non-institutional credit.

st.1: Cooperative banks give over 70% of formal farm credit in India.
st.2: Moneylenders are an institutional source of agricultural credit.

x: Statements 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: scheduled commercial banks, not cooperatives, give over 70% of formal farm credit. Statement 2 is wrong: moneylenders are a non-institutional source.

st.3: The National Commission on Farmers suggested abolishing regulated markets altogether.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the NCF suggested a regulated market within about 5 km of farmers.

st.2: The Warehousing (Development and Regulation) Act was enacted before the Central Warehousing Corporation was set up.
st.3: The FCI accredits warehouses and negotiable warehouse receipts.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the WDR Act came in 2007, long after the CWC (1957). Statement 3 is wrong: warehouses and NWRs are accredited by the WDRA.

st.1: The 14th Finance Commission award came before the enactment of the AP Reorganisation Act.
st.3: The YSR Congress left the NDA over the Special Category Status row in 2018.

x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the AP Reorganisation Act (2014) came before the 14th FC award (2015). Statement 3 is wrong: it was the TDP that left the NDA over SCS in 2018.

st.2: The Consolidated Sinking Fund is invested in the equity of State PSUs.
st.3: The Guarantee Redemption Fund is administered by the CAG.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the CSF is invested in Government of India securities. Statement 3 is wrong: the Guarantee Redemption Fund is administered by the RBI.

st.2: The 16th Finance Commission set the fiscal deficit at 3% of GDP for both the Union and the States.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the 16th FC set 3% of GSDP for the States but 3.5% for the Union.

st.2: Pensions are divided on the area ratio under Section 59.
st.3: Floating loans not raised for one State are borne wholly by the residuary State of Andhra Pradesh (Section 55).

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: pensions are divided on the population ratio (58.32 : 41.68). Statement 3 is wrong: such floating loans are divided by population ratio.

st.2: IISER of Andhra Pradesh is located at Visakhapatnam.
st.4: Only about half of the 11 national-level institutions promised to Andhra Pradesh are functional.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: AP's IISER is at Tirupati. Statement 4 is wrong: all 11 national-level institutions are functional.

st.2: Guntur Mirchi Yard is Asia's largest turmeric market.
st.3: An Agri Export Zone for turmeric has been proposed in Guntur.
st.4: Under the pulpwood trading system of February 2016, bamboo is sold to paper mills through market committees.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Guntur Mirchi Yard is Asia's largest chilli market. Statement 3 is wrong: Guntur's Agri Export Zone is for red chillies. Statement 4 is wrong: the pulpwood system covers subabul, eucalyptus and casuarina, not bamboo.

st.3: Polavaram is a State project executed under Jalayagnam without national-project status.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Polavaram has national-project status.

st.1: Employment Creation Subsidy up to 10% of Fixed Capital Investment, only for units with 5 or fewer workers
st.3: Fixed Capital Investment includes the cost of land

x: Item 2 is correct. Item 1 is wrong: the Employment Creation Subsidy is for units with more than 5 workers. Item 3 is wrong: Fixed Capital Investment excludes land.

st.1: JICA's conceptual plan (2016) identified four nodes - Visakhapatnam, Kakinada, Gannavaram-Kankipadu and Srikalahasti-Yerpedu.
st.3: The trunk infrastructure of the Kopparthy node, whose Phase-1 covers 2,596 acres, is being funded through JICA.
st.4: The 2,002-acre Bulk Drug Park is part of the Chittoor node.

x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the four-node conceptual plan was ADB's. Statement 3 is wrong: VCIC funding is from the ADB, not JICA. Statement 4 is wrong: the Bulk Drug Park is in the Visakhapatnam node.

st.2: In the Hurun Global Unicorn Index 2026, India ranked ahead of China with 61 unicorns.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: India ranked 4th with 61 unicorns, behind China.
All three statements are correct: the NAPCC (30 June 2008) has eight missions, including Green India and Sustainable Agriculture, and India announced Long-Term Ecological Observatories at COP-21.

st.3: The longest total solar eclipse of the 21st century occurred on 22 July 2009.

x: All three statements are correct: a lunar eclipse happens at full moon, a solar eclipse at new moon, and the longest total solar eclipse of the century was on 22 July 2009 (15 January 2010 was the longest annular one).

st.2: Its synodic month is about 29½ days.

x: Both statements are correct: the Moon's rotation equals its revolution, and its synodic month is about 29½ days (27 days 7 hours 43 minutes is the sidereal month).

st.1: Day and night are a consequence of the rotation of the Earth.

x: All three statements are correct: day and night result from rotation (the tilt causes seasons), the circle of illumination divides day from night, and the Coriolis force deflects winds to the right in the Northern Hemisphere.

st.2: Delhi, lying north of 23½°N, receives it once a year.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Delhi lies north of the Tropic of Cancer and never gets the overhead noon Sun.

st.3: During the Southern Hemisphere's summer, the South Pole is tilted towards the Sun.

x: All three statements are correct: January is the Southern Hemisphere's hottest month, Christmas falls in Australian summer, and in that season the South Pole tilts towards the Sun.

st.3: Laterite soil covers more of it than black soil.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: laterite covers only about 1% of AP's cultivated land, far less than black soil (about 25%).

st.2: CSIR-NIO mapped a canyon system called the 'Visakha Canyon' off Kovvada.
st.3: The Raman Seamount, about 1,505 m high, lies on the floor of the Bay of Bengal.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: NIO mapped a new canyon system off Kovvada, but there is no 'Visakha Canyon'. Statement 3 is wrong: the Raman Seamount is on the Arabian Sea floor.

st.3: Lithuania borders Belarus.
st.4: Panama borders Venezuela.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct: Lithuania borders Belarus (not Ukraine). Statement 4 is wrong: Panama borders Colombia and Costa Rica, not Venezuela.
Both statements are correct: the Thar spans India and Pakistan, and the Great Victoria is Australia's largest desert.

st.1: The Zambezi drains into the Indian Ocean.

x: All three statements are correct: the Zambezi flows into the Indian Ocean, Victoria Falls is on the Zambia–Zimbabwe border, and the Kariba Dam is on the Zambezi.

st.2: The atmosphere largely absorbs long-wave terrestrial radiation.

x: All three statements are correct: the atmosphere lets short-wave sunlight through but absorbs long-wave terrestrial radiation, and without it the Earth would average about −18°C.
Both statements are correct: peninsular rainfall decreases from west to east, and the eastern side of the Western Ghats is the leeward, rain-shadow side.

st.2: It was developed by the Bergen School of Sweden.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Bergen School is in Norway.

st.2: The taiga biome is associated with laterite soils.
st.3: Taiga forests consist mainly of broadleaf hardwoods.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: taiga soils are podzols; laterite is tropical. Statement 3 is wrong: taiga forests are mainly coniferous softwoods.

All three statements are correct: a negative IOD reduces Indian rainfall and favours Bay of Bengal cyclones, a positive IOD favours Arabian Sea cyclones, and the IOD is independent of ENSO though it interacts with it.

st.2: The thermocline off Peru deepens and the upwelling of cold water weakens.

x: All three statements are correct: at El Nino onset the trade winds weaken or reverse, the thermocline off Peru deepens and upwelling weakens, and the sea there warms by up to about 10°C.

st.3: Trewartha's 'Am' denotes the tropical savanna of the Peninsula.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Trewartha's 'Am' is the tropical monsoon climate of the west coast; the Peninsula's savanna is 'Aw'.

st.2: Assam is among the eight highly vulnerable States of the DST report (2021).

x: All three statements are correct: Jharkhand is the most vulnerable State, Assam is among the eight highly vulnerable States (Andhra Pradesh is not), and adaptation spending was about 5.6% of GDP in FY22.

st.4: By January 2020 India had cut HCFCs by 44% against a target of 35%.

x: All four statements are correct: the Kigali Amendment was adopted in 2016 and came into force on 1 January 2019, the Vienna Convention and Montreal Protocol were the first universally ratified treaties, and India cut HCFCs by 44% against a 35% target.

st.3: Perigean tides occur when the Moon is closest to the Earth.

x: All three statements are correct: semi-diurnal tides are the most common, neap tides occur when the Sun and Moon are at right angles, and perigean tides occur when the Moon is nearest.

st.2: Spring tides have the minimum tidal range.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: spring tides have the maximum tidal range; neap tides the minimum.

st.3: The main source of the salts in the oceans is volcanic eruptions.
st.4: Higher salinity increases the rate of evaporation of sea water.
